page: Microsoft Azure E2_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Ev4 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with hyper-threading. It features 16.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this configuration.

Performance benchmarks position the E2_v4 in the lower tiers. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores are weak, while multi-core CPU performance is poor, reflecting the limits of its dual-vCPU setup. Memory bandwidth tests show poor throughput, with read-only large block speeds at 8.21 GB/sec and write speeds at 7.37 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also in the bottom decile, with Redis achieving 1.76 million operations per second.

Qualitatively, the E2_v4 offers a cost-effective entry point for memory-intensive workloads that have modest CPU demands. The primary tradeoff is constrained processing power and memory bandwidth. This instance is best suited for lightweight, memory-sensitive workloads such as small-scale caching layers, minor database operations, or basic web serving.
